claims.statement: The right Collaboration panel keeps recorded exchanges and pending response requests visible across chats; expanding an exchange preserves the active chat and draft, while the bottom Dock presents Agent relationships.
Native material panels retain GPUI state and input ownership while AppKit supplies composition and attached-window focus handling.
Background archive-read failures preserve the last confirmed state; explicit failed checks show local feedback.

Conversation selection is read-only and shares one selection document across the text blocks of a rendered message. Copy controls show transient success feedback; selection does not span all messages.

The menu controller makes its nonactivating panel key on open without application-wide activation, and lifecycle tests require unchanged foreground application identity and a hidden workspace that remains hidden.

Native account disclosures use one Core Animation transaction to move and reveal account rows; the canvas accommodates both animation endpoints and requests the screen refresh rate without per-frame window resizing.

GPUI notifications prioritize errors, warnings and information for the bell and badge. Shared status rows use severity color with an icon and explicit wording; native menu-bar feedback keeps its compact icon and colored explanatory popover.

GPUI account problems use shared inline feedback beside the affected account without requiring a popup. Native menu-bar account feedback retains its compact icon and explanatory popover, whose closure does not clear the source.

The existing desktop exposes Project-grouped Work with existing-Agent responsibility selectors, selected scoped evidence and global review records while preserving conversations and the Collaboration panel.
Selected Work and private reviewer records load separately from bounded overview previews, retain explicit source and size limits, and do not treat cache or native completion as Work acceptance.

Pause Work blocks new contributions and completion without rolling back native execution; the global Save review details switch only controls observation and does not change native execution permissions.
Each independent Agent owns its displayed composer, and submitted input targets that Agent's saved conversation instead of the first root.

The existing desktop exposes explicit read-only Memory summary and Actual usage views in Agent preferences, and Actual usage in selected Work details. Source changes discard old views; copying is explicit. Unknown and shared usage and delivery versus assessment remain separate facts.

Archived and blocked conversations keep the normal locked input bar and center the shared status and recovery controls within it. The unsent draft stays saved internally and returns after recovery; the blocked bar does not repeat its text or show a duplicate status band.

Agent preferences lists at most the newest 100 retained Decodex attached-branch receipts for the exact source. Verified branch navigation preserves the source draft, uncertain creation is not repeated, and archived branches require native restoration before refresh.

Shift-Esc targets Graph or conversation fullscreen through the persistent shell, including actions forwarded from the native composer. Graph fullscreen hides both sidebars and restores their saved preferences on exit.
Parent-managed native chats expose Open parent; only failed native connections expose Retry. A positively unsent message keeps its own Not sent and Resend receipt in the scrolling transcript.
A locked conversation exposes Fork only for a readable prompt in the current native timeline binding. It creates and opens a native branch directly while preserving the original writer and draft.
Browsing or creating another conversation keeps the active call bound to its original owner and shows background call controls while preserving each conversation's draft.

The Graph groups recorded Project membership with a stable bottom rail and caption. Selecting a Project or one of its Agents highlights the rail and adds upper corners. Point overview omits small captions, and layout keeps clearance between Projects.
Settings supplies new independent conversation defaults; the input-bar shield selects current native permissions and the model menu includes speed, while native Subagents retain native inheritance.

The existing conversation browser and Project-grouped Work list have independent saved status filters with an explicit All statuses reset. They intersect existing Project and search predicates, keep a selected label when rows change, and retain exact navigation, drafts and evidence ownership without sending commands or changing native/business state.

The conversation header groups each source with multiple open native Side chats. The + action creates and opens an attached branch from the selected conversation after source preparation without a second confirmation or message send. Switching preserves per-conversation drafts and closing retains the native branch.

Conversation actions use the short Fork label, with boundary, provider and no-send details in adjacent text. Persistent attached conversation surfaces use Side chat and Side chats; native protocol identifiers and Git branch terminology remain unchanged.

Fork uses arrow.triangle.branch; account routing uses point.topleft.down.to.point.bottomright.curvepath in GPUI and Menu Bar with existing active and disabled states. New local Agent records retain Fork or Side chat identity suffixes; native conversation topics update separately. Main stays fixed and Side chat tabs use current topics, with numbered labels before a title is available.

Fork, Retry and Unarchive share settings_button sizing, border, radius and interaction feedback. Status copy wraps within its rail. Fork starts creation after source preparation without a second confirmation or Cancel control; conversation progress and recovery use the band above the composer, and creation sends no message.

Nonblocking conversation feedback uses the band above the composer; send restrictions and archive status use the disabled composer. History retry and summary notices reuse shared inline feedback. Persistent and animated local feedback share a compact inset row with a quiet tone fill, icon and explicit wording, with text, icons and recovery actions vertically centered. Field and operation failures stay beside their controls, login-item and sleep-setting recovery actions stay inside their feedback rows, app-wide events use the notification center, whole-page startup failure uses the shared status row, and Menu Bar retains compact native feedback.

Assistant remains built in and always available. RAGFlow shares lifecycle controls, full version readback, details and inline feedback with other components. Install checks Docker and Compose, prepares the service, and opens its editor. Each model accepts an independent OpenAI-compatible Base URL, optional masked API key and custom model ID. Save verifies both choices and initializes Memory automatically. Chat import starts off and remains a separate choice.

RAGFlow setup applies to the current local service profile and selected Assistant. Profile, runtime or role changes clear temporary setup presentation without replacing the chat draft; generated credentials and raw scope IDs are not Components fields, and operation feedback uses the shared inline presentation.
Pending Assistant context confirmation is presented through shared inline feedback in Work, outside the RAGFlow connection editor.

The six Settings sections are General, Agents, Appearance, Components, Accounts and Diagnostics. They share a 620-point content column and normal App typography with visible descriptions. New conversations has two rows: Permissions shows its selected mode's meaning and all four explanations in the menu, while Speed uses the existing segmented control and selected-speed usage. Context defaults and Assistance retain their native settings owners. General contains Background controls and the app version with the native update action; Updates has no separate navigation entry.

RAGFlow's direct editor has one row per model, with model ID, Base URL and optional API key above 24-point inputs. Save is the single submit label; empty required fields disable submission and complete invalid input receives inline validation. Each blank key retains only its model's saved credential at its unchanged Base URL. Collapse keeps input; Cancel clears it and errors before collapse. API compatibility, model roles, Codex memory and import consequences remain visible.

Settings uses shared quiet group surfaces, divided rows and distinct section, label, value and help roles. Setting names use medium weight. Help explains a choice, scope, cost, data effect, compatibility limit or recovery action; self-explanatory controls avoid duplicate captions. Accounts retains compact rows within one list surface. Component names, versions and lifecycle actions share one row. Expanded component, MCP and Diagnostics content uses the shared inset detail surface. Model verification and Add account use shared primary buttons; feedback stays with its operation.

A collapsed Codex setup failure shows a concise state and directs the user to its setup error. Expanding Codex shows the original complete error; Retry setup retains the existing runtime preparation owner.

The Settings permission picker keeps transient state and option focus handles in the window and reuses the existing permission rows. Arrow keys cycle within the options. Escape dismisses the menu and restores trigger focus; repeated Escape leaves Settings open. Tab and Shift-Tab dismiss the menu and continue navigation. Command-W or the window close button closes Settings, including while the menu is open. The visible trailing edge aligns with the trigger, excluding the shared shadow gutter.

Settings destinations bypass page-arrival fading. Accounts, Components, Diagnostics and Tool catalog cache share the interruptible 200 ms disclosure animation with conversations; Agent preferences uses the same catalog panel. The opening frame resolves width at zero height. Moving details measure current content before sibling layout and clip prepaint and paint to revealed bounds without a previous-frame height cache or model notifications. The same flow box includes child margins in measured and settled layout. Initially open and settled details use normal full-height layout. Completed collapse removes parent gaps. The GPUI clock drives motion, reversal preserves the current position, and reduced motion applies the target directly. Arrival on other destinations changes opacity without moving hit targets.

Each GPUI account summary places its identity, a fixed-width quota column and management actions on one compact row. One or two quota windows use the same summary height. Not-applicable windows are omitted while unknown usage keeps its row. Expanded activity retains a two-column label/value grid with current and best streak together, followed by the daily chart and a separate Reset cards area. Metric labels and values share the quota text size and muted color. Values use tabular figures without extra size or weight, and the daily chart uses a subdued accent.
Settings navigation places the selection background at the selected destination immediately. Standalone Settings tests check first-frame selection and stable content bounds across subsequent frames.
The GPUI account summary owns the disclosure click target and hand cursor. Expanded activity is an ordinary reading area; clicking its metrics does not collapse the account.

The standalone Settings window configures its material before activation. Regression tests check stable first-entry geometry, intermediate expansion and collapse, repeated toggles, interruption, clipping, live content changes, child margins and no idle frame requests.

Diagnostics shows one normal-size overall status flow and three group summaries before disclosure. Unchecked Codex checks are explicit without a redundant Run checks caption. Connection changes and recovery information remain explicit. Technical details retains every result and warns when a report is cached. Uniform groups share one status; mixed groups retain per-item statuses. Stale reports cannot supply current summaries or unchecked-check guidance; native process values keep aligned columns and explicit missing-value labels.

Appearance places all theme previews in the Settings page's single scroll area. Names wrap instead of truncating, and no inner theme scroll area captures wheel input. Color scheme help is shown when System is selected.

Component rows retain complete reported versions, including original prefixes, punctuation, build metadata and Git describe suffixes. RAGFlow's release channel is a separate Nightly detail. The receipt and UI retain its server-reported version directly without a legacy wrapper conversion.

Component status lights use existing runtime, plugin, Research and RAGFlow state. RAGFlow is green only with a responding public service API and configured Memory; disabled or incomplete setup is amber, operations blue, failures red, and unchecked or absent components gray. Tooltip and accessibility text explain each light. Public RAGFlow checks run in the background on initial inspection and Components entry with a three-second limit, without model requests or loading rows.
